methods.notes: Match the 0xFE24 service (and Yale company id 0x01D1). The lock is then driven over BLE once the offline key + slot are supplied.

device.name: Yale Access / August Smart Locks
device.notes:
August / Yale Access smart locks (August Smart Lock, Pro, Wi-Fi Smart Lock, Yale Assure with a Yale Access module). There is no official local API — the vendor posture is closed — but direct BLE lock/unlock works once a client holds the lock's OFFLINE KEY and key slot (index). Those must be pulled from an August/Yale account (a cloud login), after which day-to-day unlock is fully local. yalexs-ble is the reference local implementation (Home Assistant's "Yale Access Bluetooth").
GATT: primary service 0000fe24-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb; write bd4ac611-0b45-11e3-8ffd-0800200c9a66, read bd4ac612-..., secure-write bd4ac613-..., secure-read bd4ac614-.... Yale company id 0x01D1 (465).
FRAMING: HomeKit-derived (HAP). Plaintext frames begin 0x06, encrypted frames begin 0x11; responses are a fixed 18-byte frame. Command opcodes: 0x02 GETSTATUS, 0x03 WRITESETTING, 0x04 READSETTING, 0x0A UNLOCK, 0x0B LOCK, 0x2D LOCK_ACTIVITY.
CRYPTO/AUTH: a secure handshake exchanges two 8-byte halves — SEC_LOCK_TO_MOBILE_KEY_EXCHANGE (0x01) then SEC_INITIALIZATION_COMMAND (0x03) — which combine into a 16-byte session key; the keyIndex (slot) is submitted with the secure-session init. Session payloads are AES-CBC with a 16-byte all-zero IV, keyed by the offline key. If the key or slot is wrong the lock rejects the exchange. Motor result is read at response byte[15] (0x00 success; 0x1E-0x23 jam/mechanical failure).

openness.notes: No published local protocol; local control depends on an offline key the vendor cloud holds. The BLE stack was reverse-engineered and is mature (in production in Home Assistant). The zero-IV AES-CBC + static offline-key design has drawn security scrutiny historically; no fresh advisory URL was verified for this spec, so none is asserted here.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: There is no pairing-mode button in this flow. Authorisation is issued by the vendor account rather than by possession of the lock, which is the opposite of the Nuki model and worth knowing before someone goes looking for a button to hold.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the Yale Access app before connecting; it holds the lock while it is in the foreground.

pin.notes: The lock's OFFLINE KEY and key slot index, synchronised to a client that has logged into an August/Yale account. Per-unit key material, so no value appears here. Once held, unlocking is fully local and the account is not consulted again — which is what makes this lock survivable if the vendor service does not.

issued_to_client: The offline key + slot (synced from the August/Yale cloud account)
credentials.notes: The offline key is the crown jewel: it keys the AES-CBC session and is held by the vendor cloud, so obtaining it requires an account. The Wi-Fi variants add a separate radio/bridge; the lock core here is BLE.
stored_on_device: Offline key material + key slots (enrolled devices)

factory_reset.description:
Read the procedure for the specific model before starting: all three families below need the batteries out, and two of them need the interior escutcheon off the door to reach a button that is not externally accessible. That is deliberate on the vendor's part — a reset that could be done from outside would be a way past the lock — and it means this is not something to attempt on a door someone needs to use in the next ten minutes.
A lock previously enrolled in a Z-Wave network should be excluded from that network as well; a reset clears the lock's side but not the controller's.
factory_reset.effect: Deletes every user code including the Master code, clears enrolled clients and their offline keys, and returns all programming to factory defaults. On the Assure models, creating a new Master code is the only thing the lock will accept afterwards and must be done before anything else.

procedures.basis: Yale's installation guide for the Assure Lock 2 key-free deadbolt.
procedures.name: Assure Lock 2 Key Free Deadbolt: reset tool held for one minute

steps.action: Remove the battery cover and take out one battery.
Press the reset button for one full minute with the reset tool supplied in the hardware box.
Replace the battery and the cover.

procedures.basis: Yale's installation guide for the Assure Lock for Andersen doors.
procedures.name: Assure Lock (Andersen): reset button held across a battery insertion

steps.action: Remove the battery cover and all batteries.
Remove the interior lock body to reach the reset button, which sits above the PCB cable connectors.
Re-insert three batteries and hold the reset button for three seconds.
Still holding, insert the fourth battery and hold for a further three seconds, then release.
Re-install the interior lock on the door.
steps.expect: The lock accepts only Master PIN code creation until a new Master code is set.

procedures.name: Assure Lock SL: reset button held while the batteries go back in

steps.action: Remove the battery cover and all batteries.
Remove the interior side of the lock to reach the reset button, which sits beside the cable adapter.
Press and hold the reset button for at least three seconds while reinstalling the batteries, then release.

steps.expect: The lock accepts only Master Entry code creation until a new Master code is set.

cloud.local_alternative: Yes for control — once the offline key + slot are synced from the cloud, lock/unlock is entirely local over BLE. The offline key itself can only be obtained from an August/Yale account; there is no documented account-free way to get it.

methods.description: Obtain the lock's offline key + slot from an August/Yale account (a one-time cloud step), then run the BLE secure handshake (0x01/0x03) and send LOCK (0x0B) / UNLOCK (0x0A) as AES-CBC-encrypted frames.

steps.action: Enroll the lock in the August/Yale app and sync the account so it holds the offline keys.
Extract the offline key + key slot via the account (e.g. the yalexs integration).
Run the BLE secure handshake, then send UNLOCK (0x0A) / LOCK (0x0B) as AES-CBC frames.

setup.notes: Enroll the lock in the August/Yale app, then log the account into a client that can sync the OFFLINE KEY + key slot from the cloud (this is what Home Assistant's august/yalexs integration does; a fresh owner account may be needed to force the keys to synchronize). Hand those to a local BLE client for offline unlock thereafter.

rejoin.notes: No network membership on the lock; a client with the offline key re-connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The GATT UUIDs, HAP-derived framing, opcodes and AES-CBC (zero-IV) session crypto are from Yale-Libs/yalexs-ble; the offline-key requirement from the Home Assistant integration docs.

characteristics.name: Secure write
characteristics.notes: AES-CBC secure-session write (offline-key). Opcodes 0x0A UNLOCK, 0x0B LOCK, 0x02 GETSTATUS.

characteristics.name: Secure read
characteristics.notes: AES-CBC secure-session read; motor result at byte[15].

services.name: August / Yale lock service (0xFE24)
services.notes: HAP-derived framing (plaintext first byte 0x06, encrypted 0x11; 18-byte response). Two sessions: a plaintext Session and an AES-CBC SecureSession keyed by the offline key. Motor result at response byte[15].
